reason: subscriber.rb:94 `notifier.subscribe(pattern, subscriber)` passes the Subscriber OBJECT, which Notifications then invokes through Ruby's `#call` protocol; a JS notifier takes a callable, so trails passes `(e) => sub.call(e)`. Language shortcoming: JS has no object-answers-to-call protocol. Same substitution already ratified one file over for `log-subscriber.ts silenced? -> call`, and the wrapper's whole body is the `#call` Ruby would have made. Surfaced by the leading-underscore candidate (RFC 0106).
